about.title: A bit about me
about.lede: I’m Muaz, a Software Engineer from BRAC University in Dhaka. My main interests are backend development, web applications, and applied machine learning.
story: Most of my project work has been in Python and Flask. I’ve worked with databases, built role-based application workflows, and used OCR to extract lab values from ICU reports for my thesis.

Outside coursework, I helped organize activities with university clubs and volunteered with Ashia Foundation. Those roles gave me experience coordinating work, communicating with people, and being part of a team.
I’m looking for an entry-level software engineering, backend development, or AI/ML role where I can contribute to real projects and learn from experienced developers.

projects.title: ICU Analyzer
projects.summary: My final-year thesis: a Flask application for ICU report uploads, OCR lab-value extraction, and research into mortality-risk analysis.
projects.description: My final-year thesis explores mortality risk and health suggestions for critical patients using extended LSTM and CNN approaches. The application connects ICU report uploads, OCR-based lab-value extraction, risk analysis, consultation, and document sharing in one workflow.
projects.challenge: Connect unstructured ICU reports with a usable research workflow for patients, doctors, and administrators.
outcomes: Developed report upload and OCR-based lab-value extraction workflows to support mortality-risk analysis and health suggestions.
Designed separate admin, doctor, and patient workflows with verification, secure login, dashboards, report review, profiles, and communication.
Proposed a hybrid CNN and LSTM/BiLSTM approach and prepared requirements, diagrams, testing, ethics, limitations, and future-work documentation.
projects.limitations: This is an academic research prototype. The hybrid model is a proposed approach; no clinical validation, deployment approval, or model-performance claim is presented here.

projects.title: LifeLine
projects.summary: A course group project that helps people post requests, offer help, find nearby activity, and communicate through real-time chat.
projects.description: LifeLine is a course group project built around community help. Requests and offers include urgency and location information, while interactive maps, chat, availability indicators, suggestions, and trust badges help people connect.
projects.challenge: Make community requests and offers easier to discover and support timely communication between people.
outcomes: Contributed to requests and offers with urgency and location fields, interactive maps, availability indicators, and trust badges.
Worked with Flask, SQLAlchemy, Flask-Migrate, Flask-SocketIO, session/JWT authentication, and SQLite/PostgreSQL.
Contributed to a collaborative web application using Jinja templates and Render deployment.
projects.limitations: Developed as a course group project. The linked repository represents the team’s work; this portfolio describes my contribution without claiming sole authorship.

credits.value: Community workflows, database integration, real-time communication

projects.title: Admission Lottery
projects.summary: A modular Flask web application for college admission lottery workflows, with a structured backend and deployment configuration.
projects.description: College Admission Lottery Foundation is my personal web application. The project brings together a modular Python/Flask backend, frontend assets, an API and migration structure, environment configuration, and Render deployment configuration.
projects.challenge: Organize an admission lottery application into a maintainable web project with clear application and deployment structure.
outcomes: Built a modular Python/Flask application with dedicated frontend assets.
Organized the API and database migration structure alongside environment configuration.
Prepared Render deployment configuration for the application.
projects.limitations: A personal project focused on Flask application structure and deployment configuration.

credits.label: Focus
credits.value: Modular backend development and deployment structure

projects.title: Portfolio & Content Studio
projects.summary: An interactive technical portfolio with a protected content studio, editable case studies, and a contact inbox.
projects.description: A personal portfolio built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, and CSS. Server-rendered pages read shared portfolio data, while an authenticated admin studio maintains content through an API. The interface combines a canvas network animation with interactive project walkthroughs.
projects.challenge: Make technical work easy for recruiters to assess while keeping content editable without changing components.
outcomes: Connected the homepage introduction, headline, tagline, and technology strip to the same data used by the admin content API.
Built project case studies, a filterable archive, contact form and inbox, and a downloadable résumé into a responsive interface.
Implemented signed admin sessions, local JSON persistence and optional Redis storage, plus animated technical visuals with motion controls.
projects.limitations: A personal portfolio built with Next.js and TypeScript, with an admin panel for updating content.
